# Ticketing

This repository's work is planned and tracked in a ticketing system. The planning skills in
`.claude/skills/` (`/plan-steps`, `/plan-go`, `/plan-verify`, `/report`, `/respond` and their
variants) reach it through `bun .claude/skills/plan-steps/tk.ts`, authenticated by `TICKETING_PAT`
in `.env`. Never print, paste or commit that token.

## Agile groupings

- Sprints hold stories, stories hold tasks (tickets). Agents never create or manage sprints and never
  send `sprintId`; a new ticket joins the current sprint by itself.
- A plan is a story: a master ticket, a planning ticket, step tickets and, for multi-wave plans,
  barrier tickets. A released plan waits for a person's **Confirm plan** before it runs.
- Estimates are points only; the server derives token estimates.
- A plan's master may carry `**Effort:** very high|high|medium|small`; the header is read only on
  the master, and only the auto worker reads the effort, to choose the model. A plan request carries
  an effort too, as a field a person sets or the auto worker estimates: `tk.ts plan next` prints it
  as an `Effort:` line — one set by a person is the master's, an estimated one is its default.
  A planner (and the auto worker's estimate) chooses at most High; Very High, the only effort that runs on Fable, is a
  person's choice on the master ticket or the plan request, and tk.ts records a planner's `very high` as High.

## Getting and working tickets

- Agents obtain tickets only through `tk.ts next` (or by claiming children of a ticket they hold).
  A story taken by another agent is never touched. Taking a story assigns its open agent tickets to
  the taker — the story's hold, not work in progress; they are still pulled through `tk.ts next`.
- Once released, a ticket is read-only for agents: comments, transitions and new tickets only — no
  edits to its content, estimates or assignment.
- A question for a person is a human ticket filed with `tk.ts ask`; it pauses the story until it is
  answered. A finding that needs no decision is a report (`tk.ts report file`) and pauses nothing.
- A failing test is classed before it is touched (`tk.ts plan tests` says whether its file is the
  story's own or foreign): the story's own test or a mechanical failure is fixed — inside the ticket
  or through a fix ticket, `tk.ts fix --class story|technical` — and a failure that means a business
  rule changed without a decision is a question, `tk.ts ask --class business-logic`, which pauses the
  story until a person answers; the next run then applies the answer through a fix
  (`tk.ts fix --answers <question>`) and continues. In doubt, ask.
- Every agent reports its chat session id (tk.ts reads it from the environment); never invent one.
- A ticket title is limited to 256 characters: the server refuses a longer one (400
  `validation_failed` on `title`), so keep every title an agent writes within it.
- A plan request may arrive without a title — a person can file one from its description alone, and
  the server shows a provisional title until it is named. `tk.ts plan next` then prints
  `Title: none` and the planner names the request: `tk.ts plan open --request <key>` does it with
  the plan's title, `tk.ts plan title <request> <title>` does it explicitly. An agent never renames
  a request a person titled.

## Where work integrates

- Every agent comment names a pushed commit the server verifies on the sprint's repository, and a
  ticket is done only when a commit of it is on the sprint's configured branch.
- The sprint's configured repository and branch are the **only** source of truth for where work
  integrates. Read them with `bun .claude/skills/plan-steps/tk.ts me`; never write a branch name into
  a skill, a plan or a ticket, because a person can reconfigure the sprint at any time.
- `tk.ts push <key>` and `tk.ts done <key>` do the integration; agents commit only their own
  ticket's files.
